transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

Um, thanks, doctor. I guess what made me finally bring it up is my eating’s been kind of off the last few weeks. It’s probably not a huge thing, but I’ll realize I skipped breakfast and lunch without really meaning to, and then at dinner I just sort of pick at it—even when my wife cooked. My jeans have started feeling a little loose, so… I figured I should maybe ask about it, if that makes sense.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy lately?

Yeah… I mean, not like I can’t function or anything, but most days lately I wake up feeling kind of heavy and flat. The apartment feels really quiet, if that makes sense. Even stuff I usually like, like picking up my guitar, doesn’t really do much for me right now. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How long have you been feeling this way, with the low mood and loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?

Um… I’d say about three weeks, maybe a little more? It kind of started after my wife settled into her full-time work schedule. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but that’s when I noticed I was feeling like this most days.
Have you noticed any other changes in how you’re feeling lately, like trouble sleeping, feeling worse about yourself, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living?

Um… sleep, yeah, a little. I am sleeping, so it’s not like I’m up all night or anything, but it’s been kind of broken up. I’ll wake up around four or five and start thinking about bills or tracks I haven’t finished, and then I can’t really settle back in. So by the time the day starts I already feel tired, if that answers it.
Have you been feeling worse about yourself lately, maybe feeling like you're not good enough or blaming yourself for things?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’m, like, beating myself up all day or anything. Maybe I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I think that’s pretty normal, right? I haven’t really noticed it as a big thing.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or fidgety lately?

Maybe a little slower, yeah. Not in some huge way, I don’t think, but… everything feels kind of delayed. Like I’ll have my laptop open and just sit there for ages before I even move my hands to type or plug in the keyboard. I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living or had any thoughts of harming yourself?
No… I mean, I don’t think so. I get overwhelmed and tired of dealing with things sometimes, but I haven’t been thinking about hurting myself or anything like that. I’m okay in that sense, I think.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in your appetite, or have you lost weight without trying recently?

Yeah… a little, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but my eating’s been kind of off the last few weeks. I’ll realize I skipped breakfast and lunch without really meaning to, and then at dinner I just sort of pick at it, even if my wife made something. And my jeans are feeling a bit looser lately, so… I guess that counts?
Have you noticed a decrease in pleasure or interest in most activities, not just your usual ones?

I’m not really sure. I mean, maybe I’m less excited about things, but I wouldn’t say I’ve lost interest in everything or anything. I still… I don’t know, I can still do stuff if I need to. Maybe I just haven’t been paying close enough attention to that. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed that your movements or speech have become significantly slower, to the point where other people might notice it?

A little, yeah. I mean, I don’t know if it’s obvious to other people, but everything feels slower right now. Like I’ll sit there with my laptop open for ages before I even move my hands to type, or plug in the keyboard. It’s not like I’m trying to be lazy or anything… it just takes me longer to get moving. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed a loss of energy or felt fatigued more easily lately, even when you haven’t done much physically or mentally?

I don’t think so… not in a major way. I mean, I’ve been a little low-energy here and there, but I don’t know if it’s more than anyone would feel. I can still get through the day, mostly. I guess I haven’t really been tracking it—should I be noticing something more specific?
Have you felt a loss of energy or felt fatigued nearly every day, even when you haven't done much physically or mentally?

I don’t think it’s been nearly every day, no. I mean, I have off moments where I feel kind of drained, but not like constant fatigue from doing nothing. I don’t want to overstate it. If anything, I’d say I’m just… a bit slower sometimes, but not wiped out every day. Is that a fair way to put it?
Have you noticed any trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions lately?

Yeah, somewhat. I don’t think it’s… terrible or anything, but I notice it when I’m trying to work on code or mess with a song. I’ll keep rereading the same line, or replaying the same eight bars, and I still can’t really decide what I’m supposed to do next. It’s kind of embarrassing, honestly. I don’t know if that counts as trouble concentrating or just being stuck, but it’s been happening.
Have you found it hard to focus or think clearly most days, even when you're not particularly tired or busy?

Yeah… I think so, at least some days. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but even when I’m not especially tired or slammed with anything, I’ll try to work on code or arrange a song and I just kind of get stuck. Like I’ll reread the same line over and over, or replay the same eight bars, and still can’t decide what the next step is. It’s not all day every day, but it has been noticeable. Does that answer what you mean?
Have you noticed a big drop in your interest or enjoyment in most things, to the point where almost nothing feels satisfying or worth doing anymore?

I don’t think it’s that big of a drop, no. I still get some enjoyment out of things, even if I’m not always as into them as I’d like. It’s not like almost nothing feels worth doing anymore. Maybe I have moments where I’m kind of flat or unmotivated, but I wouldn’t want to call it that severe. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?
Would you say that most days, you feel a noticeable lack of interest or pleasure in almost all activities for most of the day?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I have times where I’m less motivated or things feel kind of muted, but “almost all activities for most of the day” sounds stronger than what I’m experiencing. I still can enjoy some things once I get into them. I hope that’s answering it the right way.
Would you say that you've felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the past few weeks?

Yeah… I guess I’d say most days lately, yes. I don’t want to overstate it, but I’ll wake up with this kind of heavy, flat feeling, like the apartment feels too quiet, and even picking up my guitar doesn’t really lift it much. It’s not dramatic every second, but it’s been there a lot. Does that count as what you mean by depressed?
Would you say that you’ve experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in almost all activities, nearly every day, for the past two weeks?

I don’t think I’d say “almost all activities,” no. It’s more like things take more effort to get into, and sometimes I’m not as excited as I’d normally be, but I can still enjoy some things. So… for the past couple weeks, it hasn’t felt like a complete loss of interest or pleasure nearly every day. Does that make sense?
Would you say you’ve felt a loss of energy or felt fatigued nearly every day, even when you haven’t done much physically or mentally?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I do feel tired sometimes, but I haven’t really tracked whether it’s nearly every day or if it’s more just normal tiredness. I wouldn’t want to say yes if that makes it sound more severe than it is. Could you maybe say what you mean by fatigued?

When I ask about feeling fatigued nearly every day, I mean a persistent sense of tiredness or lack of energy that’s there even when you haven’t been doing much—have you been feeling that way most days, even if you’re not physically or mentally busy?

I’m not sure I can honestly say it’s most days. I do have sluggish days where I don’t feel like doing much, but I haven’t really noticed it being this constant tiredness even when I’ve done nothing. Maybe I’m just not paying close enough attention, but I wouldn’t want to overstate it. Does that answer it okay?
